title: Project: turret logic

exercises.title: Targeting
exercises.prompt: Finish class Turret(double x, double y, double range): bool inRange(const Target& t) const (distance <= range), and int pickTarget(const std::vector<Target>& targets) const, which returns the index of the closest target in range, or -1 if none are.

tests.hint_if_fail: 3, 4 is exactly 5 away: in range counts the edge (<=).
Measure from the turret's position, not from 0, 0.

hints: Store x, y and range in private fields.
Loop with an index: for (int i = 0; i < (int)targets.size(); i++), keep the best distance so far.

exercises.title: Cooldown
exercises.prompt: Write class Gun with Gun(double shotsPerSecond) and bool tryFire(double now): it fires (returns true) if this is the first shot or at least 1 / shotsPerSecond seconds have passed since the last shot that fired.

tests.hint_if_fail: 2 shots a second means 0.5 s between shots.

tests.call: []{ Gun g(2); g.tryFire(1); g.tryFire(1.2); return g.tryFire(1.5); }()
tests.hint_if_fail: Only shots that actually fired reset the timer.

hints: cooldown = 1.0 / shotsPerSecond. Keep a bool for 'has fired yet' and the time of the last shot.
if (!fired || now - lastShot >= cooldown) { fired = true; lastShot = now; return true; } return false;

quiz.q: Why compare dx*dx + dy*dy with range*range?
choices: It skips the slow square root and gives the same answer
quiz.why: Both sides squared keeps the comparison the same.

quiz.q: 2 shots a second means a cooldown of...
Why keep turret logic separate from the graphics?
choices: You can test it on its own and move it between engines

explain: Explain project: turret logic to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
